prompt_text: Who is the best real estate agent in Pleasanton CA to sell my house?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” agent for every seller — the right agent depends on your house, your price range, your timeline, and what level of service you want. I can help you find the best fit. A quick plan and checklist:

1) Key criteria to use when evaluating agents
- Recent sales in Pleasanton (same neighborhood / similar price range)
- Sold price vs list price and average days on market
- Marketing (professional photos, video, targeted online ads, broker tours)
- Local network and buyer database (Tri‑Valley/Alameda County connections)
- Communication style and responsiveness
- Negotiation track record and references from recent Pleasanton sellers
- Fees and contract terms (commission, cancellation, dual agency)

2) Where to look
- Search sold Pleasanton listings on Zillow, Redfin, Realtor.com and note the listing agents
- Check agent profiles/reviews on Google, Yelp, Zillow and their brokerage pages
- Look at local brokerages with strong Tri‑Valley presence (Compass, Keller Williams, Coldwell Banker, Intero, etc.) and top producers there
- Ask neighbors or your HOA for recommendations

3) Questions to ask when you interview agents (pick 6–8)
- How many homes have you sold in Pleasanton in the last 12 months? Any in my neighborhood/price range?
- What is your average sale price vs list price and average days on market?
- What’s your marketing plan for my property? (photos, video, social ads, email list, open houses)
- How will you determine my listing price? Can I see a current CMA?
- Who will be my main point of contact and how often will you communicate?
- What are your fees and any other seller costs I should expect?
- Can you provide 2–3 recent seller references in Pleasanton?
- How do you handle multiple offers and appraisal/inspection negotiations?

4) Red flags
- Vague answers about recent local sales or marketing
- No references or unwillingness to show results
- Pushy pressure to sign immediately without a clear plan
- Poor online presence or listings with low-quality photos

5) Next steps I can help with
- If you share the property address, target price, and timeline I can draft an email/phone script to contact agents
- I can give a shortlist of what to look for in each agent’s recent sales (if you paste links to listings)
- I can draft the interview questions into a printable checklist for your meetings

If you want, tell me your address or neighborhood, target price, and how quickly you need to sell — I’ll help you prepare a shortlist and message templates to contact top local agents.
